newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian police clash with fleeing civilians.
newsitem.headline: Albanian police clash with fleeing civilians.

text.p: Scores of Albanian police clashed with about a thousand civilians trying to flee the country at the southern port of Durres on Sunday, witnesses said.
The police beat some civilians and fired hundreds of Kalashnikov rounds over their heads to drive them back from the gates of the port, which is Albania's largest.
"We are not killing the people because they are our brothers, but we have to guard the port," explained one beleaguered policeman.
"The people are coming here because they hope to go to Italy but there is no ship for them."

The Albanian civilians, mostly young men, cursed and threw stones at the police. One of the would-be refugees was carried away unconscious after being clubbed by a policeman. Another man was arrested.
Those incidents occurred after the crowd of civilians ripped down a section of iron fence and surged into the port.
About 40 police then retreated, firing into the air. They quickly mounted a counter-charge and drove the crowd back into the square by the city's train station.
The police were handling the situation with restraint but the possibility that confrontations could quickly escalate out of control clearly worried some security force members.
"We are worried someone in the crowd may get a gun and use it and that would change everything," a policeman told Reuters.
One policeman was killed in Durres on Saturday after being shot by a man on the street who resisted being searched.

Sunday marked the third straight day of unrest at the port. Albanians desperate to escape several weeks of lawlessness across the country have come to Durres in the hope of securing a berth on a ship.
A Greek frigate docked briefly in Durres on Sturday to pick up Chinese and Iranian diplomats evacuating Albania.
The ship's arrival caused a riot among civilians who broke through police lines and raced on foot two kilometres to the end of the quay where the vessel was moored.
By the time the mob arrived the ship had loaded its diplomatic passengers and was steaming away into the Adriatic.
Civil unrest swept across much of Albania in recent weeks after nine pyramid schemes collapsed, wiping out the life savings of many of the country's families.
A new coalition government has been formed to try to restore civil order through national elections in June.
Southern Albania, where pyramid losses were the greatest, is in the control of local committees -- generally referred to as rebels forces. The government still has a grip on the north.
Durres was chaotic on Thursday but the police managed to reassert their control. Most local residents seem satisfied that government security forces are necessary to preserve order.
